critical_steps: The block operator I on R(K) direct-summed with the backward shift on R(K)-perp is surjective but not injective.
The singleton atom in R(K) is a Parseval K-frame of zero excess and is fixed by the block operator.
All three excesses in the source's comparison are therefore zero.
For a finite-excess projected frame, the synthesis-kernel exact sequence shows that only the kernel of the restriction to R(K) changes the excess.
integrity.proof_basis: Exact block-operator counterexample on a one-dimensional operator range plus an exact sequence of synthesis kernels.
integrity.unproved_limits: No universal projected-excess identity is asserted for arbitrary K-frames.

scientific_limitations: The finding refutes the only-if direction of Corollary 5.11 and does not reassess unrelated theorems in the source.
The exact additive excess formula is asserted in the finite-excess regime; infinite cardinal equality can conceal a nonzero kernel dimension.
The counterexample intentionally has all atoms in R(K), so it is independent of known failures of projected-excess identities for arbitrary K-frames.
A nonindexed erratum, thesis remark, or informal correction may contain the same restricted-injectivity observation.
title: K-frame excess cannot detect noninjectivity outside the operator range
